Coverage also includes aligned tables, flags, growth with cap, multi-device errors, malformed tables/records, permissions, rollback, empty PATH, output failures and FD cleanup. lpr.note: Submit copies a job into a spool opened with O_NOFOLLOW that must be owned by the caller and not writable by group or other (a new spool is created 0700), and runs BASHLPR_BACKEND as an absolute path with a literal argv. The job counts only when the backend exits 0 and stdin reached the job size. A missing or relative backend fails before spooling. Cancel writes one byte to the control FIFO and does not signal a pid from a sidecar file; tests/secreview-lpr-cancel-identity.py checks that such a pid stays live. Listing refuses a symlink, a directory owned by another user, or a group or other writable directory. A readdir error closes the directory and fails the list, so unread jobs are not reported as an empty spool. tests/secreview-shell-fds.py runs 40 list cycles with /proc/$$/fd unchanged. SIGPIPE is ignored only around the cancel write and the caller disposition is restored.

git.note: The recorded parity run covers 69 scenarios and 414 comparisons. Dedicated integrity and apply-path regressions cover malformed storage, preflight failures, complete long patch lines and nested rename strip levels; this is not full Git compatibility. Apply rejects a patch whose work-tree path does not fit in 4096 bytes, for additions, deletions and both rename sides, with no partial write. With -pN on a path that has fewer leading directories than N, apply strips what it can and writes the last component; git 2.47.3 rejects that header and writes nothing. No registered test covers that difference. Each git command runs in a forked child, so the transport's signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) does not reach the caller; tests/secreview-shell-sigpipe.py runs ls-remote against a far end that exits at once and gets status 128 with the caller's PIPE trap and ignored and caught signal sets unchanged. A program the git child execs, such as an editor, a bisect run script or an ssh transport, gets the caller's SIGPIPE disposition back, not the transport's ignore; the git-target case checks the transport program's own bit. Non-POSIX wait runs a queued SIGCHLD trap after waitchld returns and before the next wait. POSIX wait still returns 128+SIGCHLD.
git.next: No new seven-sample timing claim. Full Git lifecycle was not rerun under ASan.

pkg.note: Index verification uses the same byte buffer that is published. Every verb except pack, delta-make and delta-apply runs contained when --root names a directory other than /: each path component below the root is opened with O_NOFOLLOW, so a symlink there is neither read nor written through. The --root prefix itself, the package file and a local source may be reached through a symlink. When the root is / (the default, or any all-slash spelling) pkg does not contain, and every link there is the administrator's and is followed. Legacy extract skips links in the package. tests/pkg-symlink-root.py refuses install, legacy extract and verify through a symlinked component, accepts a symlinked package directory and root prefix, and follows a moved package-state link under / inside a private user and mount namespace, skipping that case where none can be made; tests/pkg-sanitize.sh runs it under ASan and UBSan. When the curl builtin is not enabled, fetch falls back to an execvp PATH search for curl; no absolute downloader is configured. The server, desktop and full profiles include the curl builtin. With an empty PATH that search tries the current directory, as bash's own command lookup does. tests/secreview-shell-fds.py runs 40 pkg list --root cycles with /proc/$$/fd unchanged. Separate trust and package-publication fixtures cover signature lookup, trust-file failures and install rollback, including sanitizer checks. The pkg tests install from local files and fetch nothing from a network.

nc.note: TCP socket writes use MSG_NOSIGNAL. A write to stdout or another non-socket ignores SIGPIPE for that write only and restores the caller's disposition, so a closed reader returns EPIPE. tests/secreview-shell-sigpipe.py closes stdout under default, trapped and ignored SIGPIPE and gets the write stdout error, status 1 and the caller's PIPE trap and ignored and caught signal sets unchanged; tests/secreview-nc-sanitize.sh repeats it on an ASan and UBSan module. The peer is a loopback listener owned by the test, not an external network.

pty.note: The intermediate reaper child ignores SIGPIPE and saves the caller's action. The target gets that action back before exec, so a default or trapped SIGPIPE is the default in the started program and an ignored one stays ignored. The parent's gate byte is sent with MSG_NOSIGNAL. tests/secreview-shell-sigpipe.py runs pty spawn under default, trapped and ignored SIGPIPE and finds the caller's PIPE trap and ignored and caught signal sets unchanged. Its pty-target case reads the started program's own SIGPIPE bit under the same three setups, and tests/secreview-target-disposition-sanitize.sh repeats it on ASan and UBSan modules. The suite uses a private PTY, not a physical terminal.

cron.note: cron run opens the spool with O_NOFOLLOW and requires it to be owned by the caller and not writable by group or other (a missing spool is created 0700); the atjobs and tabs subdirectories get the same check. The state file is read with O_NOFOLLOW and a symlinked state file is not replaced. The configured cron.d directory and the output directory are followed, so root-maintained links are honoured; each cron.d file must still have a valid name and be a regular, owner-readable file with no execute bits that is not writable by group or other. A job.* file is removed only when it is a regular file. tests/cron-containment.py checks a symlinked spool, a 0777 spool, an atjobs symlink and a symlinked state file on the dynamic and static shells; it does not test the followed directories. The suite runs cron run --once against private directories and does not start crond or change the host crontab.

watch.note: watch -x passes the given words to the command as its argv, running an enabled builtin of that name or else execvp, so a shell metacharacter in an argument is not evaluated. Without -x the words are joined and evaluated by the shell. tests/watch-exec.py checks the -x argv, including an argument that contains ';', and that -e stops when the command fails; it does not test the path without -x.

integrity.note: integrity opens --root as named, without O_NOFOLLOW, and opens every component below it with O_NOFOLLOW.
